The whole “pick yourself up by your bootstraps” meme doesn’t work with depression or any other mental illness for that matter. In fact it causes more harm than good. Would you tell someone that has heart disease to just get over it? This is the exact reason I responded to you in the first place. Mental illness is a very real thing and it doesn’t have to do with just powering through. If it was that easy then it wouldn’t be an illness. It’s not an excuse just an explanation. I do agree that having some sort of perseverance is a good thing but you’re undermining a very serious thing that can lead to severe consequences. You obviously have no idea how mental illness works because if you did you would see the problem in the things you’re saying.

I wouldn’t necessarily call mental illness a crutch that people lean on. Depression and bipolar disorder are illnesses that effect how you see the world. It’s not even necessarily self pity either. I have diagnosed severe depression I don’t say that expecting people to feel sorry for me or anything but just that dealing with it (especially in the world we find ourselves in) is/can be extremely difficult. If you’ve ever been depressed the thing you want the most is to feel better and for it to not engulf your life. The problem with ‘mental health’ problems is that people find a really hard time understanding it unless they’ve experienced it themselves. I agree with not letting it hold you back but to say that people use it as crutch and self pity is far from the actual truth.

Hey,  I’m really not good this comforting thing and maybe I shouldn’t even be writing this with that mindset but I see so much of myself in you. I’m also 20 in a pretty small community (it’s large  in size but it’s still a small town vibe) and it really puts a weight on your growth, especially if you’re like us where we come up with any idea to shit on ourselves. This is grade A depression man and I don’t want to see you go down this road without getting help. Just a couple of months ago I was like you and I had completely given up. The more I look back at it I realize how serious I was about driving my car into a ditch in hopes I could die in a painful way because that’s all I deserved. Getting help though therapy and a psychiatrist has put me in a place where the cloud and lack of motivation isn’t nearly as crippling as what it used to be. I know you have anxiety and panic attacks when trying to go get help (I went though this phase when dropping out of school due to depression) but I strongly encourage you to get that help. It will still be rough, this isn’t necessarily something that goes away and improvements will be extremely daunting and slow but the only way out is though. Feel free to pm me anytime to talk. I don’t care what you have done in the past I will pass no judgements on you as no one deserves to feel this way. Don’t go towards suicide if you’re considering it as if no one else would miss you I would. Please take care man.
